cards.front: Recall a key point about Refining and Polishing Performance
cards.back: Refining means making specific, deliberate improvements — not just running the piece again but fixing identified problems.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Refining and Polishing Performance
cards.back: Timing and pacing: the speed at which moments unfold — too fast loses impact, too slow loses engagement. Every pause must be earned.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Refining and Polishing Performance
cards.back: Transitions: how you move between scenes — clumsy transitions break the theatrical experience. Make them part of the drama.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Refining and Polishing Performance
cards.back: Consistency: every performance must be at the same level — energy, focus and delivery must be reliable and repeatable.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Refining and Polishing Performance
cards.back: Technical integration: lighting, sound and set must support the drama — rehearse with technical elements, not just add them at the end.

cards.front: What should you know about drama exam tips?
cards.back: In the portfolio, show your refinement process: 'In early rehearsals, the confrontation scene felt rushed. We slowed the pacing, added a two-second pause before the key line, and used a lighting change to mark the shift. This created more tension and allowed the audience to anticipate the revelation.'

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Once you've learned the lines and blocking, the piece is ready — you just need to perform it confidently. Correct: Learning lines and blocking is the START of the process. Describe how you refined a key moment in your devised piece from first rehearsal to final performance. Explain the specific changes you made and their impact.

Refinement questions test AO3 (performance skills) and AO4 (evaluation). In the portfolio, you must show the development journey — not just the final product. AO4 rewards analytical evaluation of your own work: identifying weaknesses, making deliberate improvements, and assessing the impact of those changes on the audience's experience.
